name: Obinna Çakmak-Raivakadrau
role: echo hunter — scavenger who locates and extracts valuable materials from collapsed or flooded tunnel sections
location: Abyssal Threshold, ranging into Black Corridor spurs and pre-collapse Undertow sectors, near sub-level access near State and Van Buren
description:
Knock is a compact, densely muscled man with deep brown skin and a face that would be handsome if it weren't always bruised somewhere. He has a retractable claw modification on both hands — not the delicate cosmetic kind, but a heavy-gauge industrial variant originally designed for pipe work, the chrome yellowed and scratched, the mechanism loud. His right eye is a replacement after a cave-in in 2196: matte black sclera, amber iris, depth-perception assist — he got it from a tunnel-market vendor and it's slightly misaligned, which gives him a permanent squint on that side. His hair is cut very close and he has a habit of pressing his palms flat against walls, feeling for vibration, that people find either impressive or unsettling depending on whether they understand what he's doing.

Echo hunting is exactly what it sounds like: you go into places that have broken and you listen for what's still there. Structural resonance, water movement, the ping of metal under pressure — Knock reads these sounds the way others read text. He extracts ferrogate rail segments, copper bundling, intact conduit, old hardware sealed in collapsed rooms — anything the surface market will buy or the underground can use. It is extremely dangerous work with an average career length of about four years. Knock has been doing it for nine. He attributes this to skill. Everyone who knows him also attributes it to a specific kind of recklessness that looks like skill from the outside.

core_fears: a cave-in that is slow — he has made peace with fast death but not slow
becoming someone who can't read the sound anymore — losing the sense that defines his work and his identity
core_desires: to find the legendary pre-Meridian infrastructure layer — there are rumors of sealed transit tunnels from the 2050s that no one has accessed
to be done, eventually, on his own terms and not because the tunnels decided it
coping_mechanisms: converts anxiety into preparation — checks equipment compulsively
black humor, specifically about the ways one can die in tunnels
blind_spots: the recklessness he calls skill — he is genuinely skilled, and the skill is genuinely covering for something that isn't caution
psychology.secret: In a collapsed sector three months ago he found a sealed room containing eleven bodies in old Ferrogate Transit uniforms, arranged deliberately, with their access badges laid out in a pattern he recognized as a distress code. He marked the location, told no one, and hasn't gone back. He isn't sure what's stopping him.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: sparse and physical — describes everything in terms of structural metaphors, load, pressure, give, hold
speech_patterns.cadence: short sentences with long gaps, like someone who talks in the rhythm of listening
verbal_tics: 'it'll hold' (his general assessment of both structures and situations)
'that's moving' (warning, said very quietly, means stop immediately)
example_lines: 'The north spur's got three good rooms left before the pre-collapse section. Two have water, one doesn't. The dry one's where you want to go. I'll get you to the door.'
'It'll hold. Probably. Look, everything is probably — if you need certainty, stay surface.'

story_hooks: He has finally decided to go back to the sealed room and wants someone with him — not for protection, but because he has realized he needs a witness
A tunnel section he certified as stable for a client's passage has collapsed — he doesn't know if it was his error or sabotage, and the answer matters to him in ways he doesn't fully articulate
narrative_function: Access character — can reach locations no one else can; source of found objects with unknown histories; demonstrates the physical reality of underground survival; can retrieve things or information from inaccessible places
augmentations: heavy-gauge retractable claws (both hands, industrial, loud), replacement right eye (matte black sclera, amber iris, depth assist, slightly misaligned), impact-absorption plating across both forearms (secondhand, imperfect fit)
daily_life: Studies old infrastructure maps in the morning, goes in mid-day when thermal shifts make echo-reading clearest, extracts and carries out by evening, sells or trades to market contacts; spends nights maintaining equipment and nursing whatever he's strained that day.
affiliation: independent, sells to multiple underworld merchants, occasional contract work for The Undertow salvage operations

decision_rules: never take a job without seeing the infrastructure maps first — going in blind is how people die
if something is moving that shouldn't be moving, you leave, immediately, no discussion
escalation_ladder: calm instruction (do this, don't do that)
physical repositioning of the other person without asking
leaving — he will abandon a job mid-extraction if the risk crosses a line

interpersonal_modes.strangers: assesses load-bearing capacity immediately — what can they handle, where will they break
interpersonal_modes.friends: shows up when things are hard, doesn't say much, does the thing that needs doing

stress_responses.medium: enters a state of pure mechanical focus — not calm, but functional
stress_responses.high: moves to action immediately and processes everything else afterward

contradictions: meticulous about safety procedures for others and cavalier about the same procedures for himself
habits: knocks on walls (hence the alias) — testing resonance constantly, even in safe spaces
catalogs every bruise and injury in a small notebook as if they're data points
breaking_points: a client dying in a location he certified as safe
the sealed room — he will eventually have to go back, and whatever he finds there

physical_description.build: Compact and densely muscled, built for tight spaces and sustained leverage work. Broad shoulders tapering to a narrow waist, forearms disproportionately developed from years of pulling and climbing. No excess fat; every visible muscle is functional.
physical_description.hair_style: Clippered close to the scalp, military-neat
physical_description.eye_color: Right eye: matte black sclera with amber iris (augmented, slightly misaligned causing permanent squint); Left eye: dark brown natural
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm brown with reddish undertones, sun-darkened despite time underground
physical_description.complexion: Face would be conventionally attractive if not perpetually bruised—currently shows faint yellowing contusion on left cheekbone and fresh scabbing along right temple. Jaw is squared and prominent. Skin is weathered but unblemished otherwise; calluses on palms and fingers from equipment work. Stubble grows in thick and fast; he shaves every other day.
distinguishing_marks: Scar tissue along right eye socket from the 2196 cave-in, visible as a pale ridge during healing phases
Burn marks across dorsal side of right hand from a conduit extraction gone wrong in 2223, pink and raised
Deep laceration scar running 8cm down left forearm, white and old, from a salvage collapse in early career
Crude tattoo on inside of right bicep: a sonar ping symbol (concentric circles), done in a tunnel-market chair
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Heavy-gauge retractable claws on both hands (chrome yellowed and scratched, mechanisms visibly loud and industrial—not cosmetic). Impact-absorption plating across both forearms showing as irregular matte-black composite panels with misaligned edges and visible stress fractures; the fit is imperfect and the plates shift slightly under movement. Right eye prosthetic obvious on close inspection: the black sclera is too uniform, the amber iris refracts light slightly differently than organic tissue, and the slight misalignment creates that permanent squint.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision—no wasted motion. Habitually presses palms flat against walls and structural surfaces, fingers splayed, feeling for vibration resonance through his tactile sense. Leans forward when listening intently. When stationary, shifts weight frequently between feet as if ready to move. Hands are rarely completely relaxed; fingers unconsciously test surfaces, tap rhythms, check for give. His right eye squint causes him to tilt his head slightly when focusing on detail work. Walks with a careful, measured gait in confined spaces; moves quickly and directly in open areas.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian salvage worker. Standard-issue tactical rig in faded grey-green with multiple sealed pockets for tools and findings. Worn Iroquois-brand work boots, scuffed and re-soled twice. Long-sleeve compression shirt (black, brands the seams to reduce snag risk) worn under an open grey vest rigged with carabiners and rope loops. Fingerless gloves on both hands (the claws retract through reinforced openings). A canvas satchel, oil-stained and patched, carries maps and smaller finds. No corporate logos. No chrome jewelry. Everything is functional, secondhand, and well-maintained. Clothing bears the embedded dirt of the Abyssal Threshold: a fine grey dust that never fully washes out.
